original_question: Let Ω be a Polish space. We call a semigroup T = (T (t))t≥0 of contractions on Cb (Ω) a transition semigroup if (i) for every f ∈ Cb (E) we have T (t)f → T (s)f locally uniformly whenever t → s and (ii) for every t ≥ 0 and every uniformly bounded sequence (fn )n∈N ⊂ Cb (Ω) that converges locally uniformly to f , we have that T (t)fn converges locally uniformly to f . Is there a characterization of the generators of such a semigroup akin to the Lumer–Phillips theorem?
correct_elements: The draft already captures the correct open problem very closely: it has the right ambient setting (a Polish space Ω), the right function space C_b(Ω), the two continuity/compatibility conditions used to define the paper’s transition semigroups, and the correct goal of seeking a Lumer–Phillips-type generation theorem.
missing_details: The notation should be normalized to C_b(Ω); the draft inherits the paper’s inconsistent occurrence of C_b(E) in condition (i).
It should be stated that “contractions” means with respect to the supremum norm on C_b(Ω).

To make the definition self-contained, it should be explicit that these semigroups are not assumed strongly continuous in the sup norm; the continuity required is only local-uniform in the spatial variable.

Condition (ii) should be written in a mathematically stand-alone continuity form, namely that T(t)f_n converges locally uniformly to T(t)f when f_n converges locally uniformly to f and is uniformly bounded; as written in the draft (and in the paper’s displayed wording), the target limit “f” is not the natural continuity statement.

The nearby comments explain that Hille–Yosida-type characterizations of generators are already available once one views these semigroups through the strict topology β_0, so the real missing ingredient is not just any characterization but a usable Lumer–Phillips-type one.

The paper explicitly says that practicality is more important than maximal generality: even a verifiable sufficient generation criterion, possibly using extra hypotheses natural in applications such as positivity of the resolvent or a strong Feller property of the resolvent, would count as progress.
refined_question: Let Ω be a Polish space, and let C_b(Ω) be the Banach space of bounded continuous scalar-valued functions on Ω with the supremum norm. Call a semigroup T = (T(t))_{t ≥ 0} on C_b(Ω) a contraction transition semigroup if ||T(t)|| ≤ 1 for all t ≥ 0, if for every f ∈ C_b(Ω) one has T(t)f → T(s)f locally uniformly on Ω whenever t → s, and if for every t ≥ 0 and every uniformly bounded sequence (f_n) ⊂ C_b(Ω) with f_n → f locally uniformly on Ω, one has T(t)f_n → T(t)f locally uniformly on Ω. Can one formulate a usable Lumer–Phillips-type generation theorem for this class—preferably in terms analogous to dissipativity plus a range condition, and avoiding Hille–Yosida resolvent-power bounds—that characterizes, or at least gives practically verifiable sufficient conditions for, when a linear operator A on C_b(Ω) generates such a contraction transition semigroup? In the spirit of the paper, additional assumptions natural in applications, such as positivity of the resolvent or a strong Feller property of the resolvent, may be allowed.
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Section 1, Problem 3. The refinement mainly comes from incorporating the surrounding comments: the paper explains that generator characterizations are already obtainable by combining the transition-semigroup definition with β_0-equicontinuity, so the unresolved issue is specifically a practical Lumer–Phillips-style criterion rather than a generic Hille–Yosida characterization. The comments also state that usability is the priority and that even a sufficient criterion, possibly using positivity or strong Feller assumptions on the resolvent, would already be valuable. I also normalized the notation to C_b(Ω), made the norm and topology explicit, and wrote condition (ii) in the natural continuity form needed for a self-contained formulation.
